newsitem.title: FINLAND: JOUTSENO PULP COSTS TO FALL FIM 100 MLN - CEO.
newsitem.headline: JOUTSENO PULP COSTS TO FALL FIM 100 MLN - CEO.

text.p: Metsa-Botnia's 650 million markka investment programme in Joutseno Pulp which it is buying from UPM-Kymmene will lower the mill's annual costs by 100 million markka, said Metsa-Serla CEO Jorma Vaajoki.
"The investments will lower costs by 100 million markka per year," he told a news conference on Tuesday.
Its capacity would rise to 350,000 tonnes of elemental chlorine-free bleached softwood sulphate pulp per year from 320,000, Metsa-Serla said in a statement.
One of the mill's problems was an outdated liquor line with insufficient capacity and excessive emissions, it said.
UPM's CEO Juha Niemela said the unit has been running at almost full capacity and making relatively even profits over the cycle as internal supplier to UPM-Kymmene.
Neither company would give any figures on its profitability but Metsa-Serla said its average annual turnover was about 900 million markka, depending on the state of the market.
